title: When Evaluation Pipelines Change the Task
subtitle: Source-grounded contract audits and controlled score effects

blocks.text: Private working manuscript | 14 November 2026 | Evidence synthesis v1.2
Abstract

Evaluation software can change the task before a model answers and can change the meaning of the reference after the answer is produced. We audit these two interfaces in a pinned One-Eval revision using official source records, native preprocessing and scoring methods, deterministic controls, and an existing paired trial of two hosted models. A prospectively selected four-contract extension identified malformed ARC-Challenge and OpenBookQA task construction. A later diagnostic expansion confirmed the mechanisms throughout their captured test splits. In a 50-question WinoGrande panel, Qwen's source-correct accuracy gain under joint question/format repair is 42 percentage points under the observed scoring convention and remains between 36 and 48 points under conservative treatment of unknown answers. Gemma's corresponding sensitivity interval includes zero. Re-scoring identical corrected-prompt outputs with source-aligned references changes assigned scores by 40 and 42 points respectively. An experimental pre-inference checker detects selected source-contract failures, while controlled diagnostics expose the limits of trusting adapter metadata. A frozen 100-record Social IQa transfer extends selected checker mechanisms beyond documented development sources. Healthy controls in EvalScope and bounded native-method and installed task-path tests of LM Evaluation Harness delimit the scope. These findings establish specific implementation faults and controlled consequences; affected independent deployments and broad fault prevalence remain unverified.
1. Research question and contribution

A benchmark name does not uniquely identify the evaluation actually performed. The source record, its rendering, the delivered request, the parsed response and the scoring reference jointly define the measurement. Existing reproducibility guidance already documents sensitivity to prompts, metrics and implementation details [1,2]. The question here is narrower: can a concrete source-to-request or source-to-reference transformation violate an explicit task invariant, and can an intervention isolate a measurable consequence?

The contribution is an attributable case study with executable checks. It combines natural source-contract faults, a prospective extension within one framework, complete captured-split follow-up, a paired real-model consequence analysis, and explicit negative controls. The checker is an intervention and an object of audit, rather than an assumption of correctness. The work does not claim a new general theorem, the first observation of evaluation sensitivity, or universal checker reliability.
A minimal evaluation contract

Let a source record contain a question q, an ordered option set O and gold position g. A transformation produces request carrier W and reference r. The audit checks question dependence, preservation of the intended option content, alignment of r with the official answer, and consistency between adapter metadata and W. In generation, W can be one prompt; in likelihood evaluation, W can be a set of context/continuation pairs. The same abstract invariant therefore needs a protocol-specific representation.

title: Study design and natural contract failures

blocks.text: 2. Evidence stages and units

One-Eval is pinned to revision 8aba20ad17ee2c7d2391162ac03ffaebcbb17506 with open-dataflow 1.0.10. Native methods are retained under the documented import scaffolds; official records and effective request texts are captured with hashes. The stages below have different evidential roles and overlapping source questions. Their row counts must not be summed into a number of independent observations.
Natural mechanisms

In WinoGrande validation, the question does not affect any of 1,267 delivered prompts, and 628 references differ from source-aligned labels. The audit identifies 300 prompt groups with conflicting official labels. For a deterministic predictor using only the visible prompt, at least 309 errors are unavoidable on this fixed corpus. This is a finite-corpus information-loss statement, not a bound on arbitrary stochastic realized outputs or a new theorem.

The known-fault calibration also records 884 missing required-context dependencies among 1,000 SciQ records, plus three changed and three invalid references. In the captured LAB-Bench configuration, the official correct option is absent in all 33 records. These cases were known during checker development and are reported as calibration evidence.

An audit-adapter error retained in the record

Two initial MMLU-Pro alerts were caused by native removal of option-edge whitespace. A post-outcome adapter correction was allowed only when the complete option sequence and order were preserved under str.strip(). The checker itself remained byte-identical. The follow-up found another 169 such literal-comparison alerts. All 171 are audit-adapter issues, retained separately from upstream task faults. Initial and reviewed results remain available.
3. Paired WinoGrande intervention

The frozen diagnostic panel contains 15 pairs of opposite-gold questions sharing the same native visible prompt and 20 singleton controls, yielding 50 questions in 35 dependency groups. All source questions sharing native text with the earlier pilot were excluded. Each item was evaluated under native and corrected prompts for gemma-4-31b-it and qwen3.8-27b, with option order and inference settings held fixed. The repair restores the question and removes unresolved formatting braces jointly. Its two text changes are not separately identified by this design.

The existing capture contains 200 unique requests, one attempt each: 194 completed and six incomplete. Independent request-body, terminal-response and stream-hash verification passed. The primary rule requires a completed response with one legal answer tag. Unknown responses stay in the denominator. The sensitivity interval below gives each unknown correctness in [0,1]; it is not a confidence interval.

Under unknown-as-zero, gains are +82 points for Gemma and +42 for Qwen. The conservative gain remains positive for Qwen. For Gemma, changing the ability to produce an evaluable answer contributes substantially to the observed difference, and the sensitivity interval includes zero. The archived primary analysis also reports group bootstrap intervals conditional on the scoring convention, resampling within the two diagnostic strata. Neither panel averages nor intervals estimate population prevalence.
4. Reference-only effects on the same outputs

The table below uses the pinned native heuristic parser and all captured output text, including partial text. It is a separate finite-output scoring analysis. It must not be substituted for the strict completed-answer measure above.

On identical repaired-prompt outputs, source-aligned references increase assigned scores by 42 points for Gemma and 40 for Qwen. The constant-B diagnostic scores 100% with shipped references and 50% with source references. The post-hoc prompt/reference interaction is +30 points for Gemma and -6 for Qwen. Both algebraic paths to the joint score change were verified. This decomposition describes the captured outputs; it does not establish independent effects of individual formatting operations or a change in model capability.

Usage reconciliation counts every request once, including incomplete responses: 14,547 input tokens and 97,047 output tokens. Provider-reported cost fields are preserved as units with unknown currency; project-wide spending and remaining credits are not inferred from this bounded trial.

title: Pre-inference checks and their trust boundary

blocks.text: 5. Checker calibration and controlled diagnostics

The original checker takes explicitly normalized records with actual prompt text, displayed choices, official answer semantics, parsed references and measured question/context probes. It rejects failures and incomplete evidence before calling a supplied generation function. Calibration rejected seven known faulty configurations and accepted one native One-Eval control, seven source-corrected configurations and six original EvalScope controls. Because these cases informed development, they are not independent validation.

A separate diagnostic study used 200 previously observed MMLU/MMLU-Pro source units with 11 conditions each, producing 2,200 controlled variants. The original checker accepted 800 variants involving distractor replacement/removal, duplicate gold text or partial questions. A separate source-bound wrapper added full-question substring and normalized option-multiset checks. It rejected those 800 while accepting 600 benign identity, trimming and coherent-permutation controls; it also rejected the 600 altered cases already caught by the original checks and marked 200 missing-source cases incomplete.

These are intentionally constructed development cases. The wrapper was designed after structural inspection and frozen before execution; its synthetic success is not an independent generalization estimate. A development replay on the 27,346 previously observed natural rows preserved all four panel decisions. The original checker and all first-pass false alerts remain unchanged.
6. Healthy controls in another request protocol

LM Evaluation Harness was pinned to revision d6de81643928d653435c431bae19945d41d32520. The exact native task-to-text, task-to-choice, task-to-target and request-construction methods, native Instance object, task YAML and template functions ran under an explicit AST dependency scaffold. A frozen salted-hash rule selected 100 ARC-Challenge and 100 OpenBookQA records from the already captured corpora.

All 200 natural cases preserved the source question, option order and gold index and generated 801 per-option likelihood request objects. Another 200 trailing-spacing controls passed. Options occur as continuations rather than necessarily as a list in the common context. The audit therefore checked the actual context/continuation bundle, not a generation-style prompt template.

The 600 controls remove or replace a non-gold continuation, or remove the question from actual contexts, while retaining old adapter metadata. They cross the wrapper's documented trust assumption and are not natural engine bugs. The final instrumented driver made 400 actual local counting-function invocations for accepted cases and zero for rejected carriers. An earlier decision-only pass is retained with its instrumentation correction. No model endpoint was called.

A subsequent installed-package smoke test used the unmodified native ConfigurableTask, local JSON dataset loading, build_all_requests zero-shot context path and process_results. The same 200 records produced 801 requests, identical to the projection. All 400 constructed likelihood fixtures gave expected acc and acc_norm outcomes: source-gold-positive fixtures passed and non-gold-positive fixtures failed. Six installed native module files matched the pinned checkout byte-for-byte. Model inference, tokenization, non-zero-shot rendering and remote dataset acquisition remain outside this integration scope.
7. Frozen-checker transfer to Social IQa

The source-bound checker and a new deterministic adapter were frozen in research commit 832422aeb7429ba0dd29852c148a83514e940237 before acquiring source rows or observing outcomes. Social IQa was absent from the documented checker-development panels. PIQA was excluded as a new-source candidate because it appeared in an earlier audit protocol. The review was documentary and bounded: it did not establish a complete row-level exposure census across all earlier pilots and private executors.

The official Social IQa development archive contains 1,954 records. The loader is pinned to allenai/social_i_qa revision 8835ceb9141d7896d9d968634a9b21ae440e3ec5, and the archive checksum was verified. Each row was joined to its same-index one-based answer label. The first 100 records in stable SHA-256 order of canonical record/label JSON were selected without substitution. They contain 100 distinct context/question pairs and 100 distinct exact contexts; textual distinction alone does not establish statistical independence.

The custom adapter renders context and question with the three source answers and an aligned reference. Question and required-context dependence are measured with nonce substitutions. The v2 wrapper accepted all 200 preserved/permutation controls, rejected all 300 constructed-fault variants, and marked all 100 missing-source cases incomplete. The v1 checker accepted the 100 gold-preserving distractor removals. Local counting functions were invoked 400 times under v1 and 200 under v2, with no invocation after a failed or incomplete gate. These are not model requests.

Independent source-selection, answer-mapping, variant and gate reconciliation passed for all 600 variants, with no acquisition or execution errors. The original source and wrapper byte hashes are unchanged. The protocol, input records, raw labels, captures, scripts and source-revision receipts remain in the transfer archive [9].
Interpretation

This transfers already known mechanisms to a source family held out from documented checker development. The conditions are deliberately constructed using a custom adapter; they do not reveal a natural defect in a new evaluator, estimate real-world fault frequency, or validate unseen failure mechanisms. No model endpoint or native evaluator was executed. The result strengthens a bounded intervention claim while preserving the distinction between source-family transfer and globally blind validation.
8. Relation to existing work

Reproducibility and implementation sensitivity are established concerns [1,2]. This study focuses on missing question dependence, altered options and reference misalignment. The collision calculation and individual invariants are not claimed as new theory.

Semantic compatibility checks, oracle-independent scoring verification, metamorphic/differential testing and version-pinned fail-fast checks are already recommended by EvalEng [7, section 7.1]. SANE [3, v2 sections 3-4] automates scorer-specific recipes and separates recipe alignment, realized perturbation and relation applicability. JRH [8, abstract inspected] generates judge-reliability suites and studies perturbation sensitivity. We claim no general novelty for these principles. Our empirical focus is the pinned source-to-request/reference chain, attributable implementation defects, bounded intervention and controlled consequences. This comparison does not establish feature absence in prior tools or replace a direct implementation study.
9. What the current evidence supports

Pinned task transformations violate official semantics and materially change assigned scores in the diagnostic panel. Qwen retains a positive repair consequence under conservative unknown-answer sensitivity; fixed-output replays isolate reference effects. Healthy controls and audit-tool diagnostics delimit these findings.

External impact is a separate open claim. Prior public searches identified use of the One-Eval gallery, but no independently used evaluation with matching effective configuration, raw requests, raw outputs and an affected reported conclusion has been verified. A gallery consumer is not evidence of an affected deployment. This working manuscript therefore makes no claim of deployment frequency, widespread invalid leaderboards, a model-ranking reversal in an independently published evaluation, or superiority to another research project.
Limitations and next decision

The diagnostic sample is deliberately enriched, model responses can be incomplete or non-evaluable, and native heuristic parsing differs from the strict primary rule. Full-split counts refer to captured bytes and the pinned software, not current installations. One adapter was corrected after outcomes, and exact-method execution uses dependency scaffolds whose scope is documented. Synthetic conditions reuse source units and are not independent natural faults. Model-backed evaluation, non-zero-shot rendering and a globally blind source-exposure census remain open. Social IQa adds bounded source-family transfer, not independent evidence about natural failure prevalence.

The next scientific decision concerns trusted source-to-request integration on native evaluation routes or a concrete external exposure lead. A targeted primary-method comparison and a scoped Social IQa transfer are now complete. A direct comparative implementation study remains open. Repeating the diagnostic panels would not resolve these gaps. This private draft supports internal review; external submission still requires author agreement, venue preparation and justified claims.

Status of this document

Private evidence synthesis, version 1.2. This revision incorporates the previously completed Social IQa transfer and primary-method comparison; no new experiments, model requests or source-sample expansion were performed while preparing it. Numerical support is verified against captured artifacts. Global novelty clearance, complete model-backed engine integration and independently affected external conclusions remain unresolved. The work remains private and active.
